issues.description: The problem statement's UML specifies Stock.take(String) returns int, and the solution implements take(String) returning int. However, the template's Stock.take method has the signature 'public boolean take(String ingredient)'. This return-type mismatch will confuse students and prevent them from following the specification or using the solution as reference when they implement SealSaloon (which expects an int-returning take in calculate/restore logic).
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template Stock.take method signature to match the specification and solution: change 'public boolean take(String ingredient)' to 'public int take(String ingredient)'. Adjust the implementation to return -1 when the ingredient is not available (or not found) and return the remaining quantity after decrement on success. This aligns the template with the UML/spec and the solution, avoiding confusion when students implement SealSaloon.
